name: Productlane
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Connect interview notes and support feedback to product issues and decisions

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 25 AI resolutions/month included; additional resolutions cost $0.79 each.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 50 AI resolutions/month included; additional resolutions cost $0.79 each.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: 100 AI resolutions/month included; additional resolutions cost $0.79 each.

tiers.name: Early Stage program, Year 1
tiers.limits: 6 full seats + 20 viewer seats; 200 AI resolutions/month.
tiers.notes: 12-month contract billed monthly. Published step-up is $451/month in Year 2 and $594/month in Year 3; eligibility includes fewer than 15 employees, under $10 million funding and no prior paid subscription.

pricing.billingTerms: Annual public seat pricing; a monthly toggle exists but exact month-to-month prices were not exposed. The Early Stage program is a non-cancelable annual contract billed monthly. A 7-day trial is offered.
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI resolutions above the included allowance cost $0.79 each; the Early Stage contract cannot be canceled before its annual term ends and rises from $65/month in Year 1 to $451/month in Year 2 and $594/month in Year 3.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Productlane, connect interview notes and support feedback to product issues and decisions. The hard boundary is linear integration, call workflows, customer portal, sync, and team collaboration, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Collect interview notes and support feedback, merge duplicates, connect evidence to product issues and decisions, and publish a transparent status or research view.
whatYouLose: Linear integration, call workflows, customer portal, sync, and team collaboration
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Productlane because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Quackback
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Connects support feedback to issues, but has no interview-note research workspace.

rejectedAlternatives.name: QualCoder
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Handles interview coding well, but has no support ingestion or product-issue linkage.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Productlane in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect interview notes and support feedback, merge duplicates, connect evidence to product issues and decisions, and publish a transparent status or research view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
